Points, Lines and Line Segments:
✏️ Points, Lines, and Segments ✏️

The tiny building blocks of the whole geometric universe!

1. Understanding a Point

A point shows an exact position or location. It has no length, width, or thickness! We usually represent it with a small dot and label it with a capital letter (like Point A).

2. Understanding a Line

A line is a straight path that extends endlessly in BOTH directions. It has no endpoints! We draw arrows at both ends to show that the line continues forever.

3. Understanding a Line Segment

A line segment is a part of a line with two fixed endpoints. It has a definite, measurable length! The straight edge of a ruler or the side of a book are examples of line segments.
Rays and Angles — Introductory:
🔦 Rays and Angles 🔦

Where lines meet, angles are born!

1. What is a Ray?

A ray is a straight path that begins at one fixed point and extends infinitely in ONE direction. Think of a beam of light travelling from a flashlight!

2. What is an Angle?

An angle is formed when two rays share the exact same endpoint. This shared endpoint is called the vertex (the corner!). The two rays are called the arms or sides of the angle.

3. Measuring Angles

An angle measures how much one arm turns away from the other. Angles are measured in degrees, using the symbol °. The size of an angle does NOT depend on how long the arms are drawn; it only depends on how wide they open, like a door!
Parallel and Perpendicular Lines:
🛤️ Parallel & Perpendicular 🛤️

Lines that never meet, and lines that crash at perfect corners!

1. Parallel Lines

Parallel lines (symbol: ∥) are straight lines that remain the exact same distance apart and NEVER meet, even if they stretch on forever! Think of railway tracks or the lines on a piece of ruled paper.

2. Perpendicular Lines

Two lines are perpendicular (symbol: ⊥) when they meet to form a perfect square corner, called a Right Angle (exactly 90°). Think of the corners of a window or the letter T!

3. Intersecting Lines

Intersecting lines are any lines that cross or meet at a point. Perpendicular lines are just a special type of intersecting lines that happen to meet at exactly 90°!
Types of Angles:
📐 Types of Angles 📐

Every angle has a special name based on how wide it opens!

1. Acute Angle

An acute angle is tiny and sharp! It is greater than 0° but less than 90°. (Think of a slightly open pair of scissors).

2. Right Angle

A right angle measures exactly 90°. It forms a perfect square corner! (Think of the corner of a book).

3. Obtuse Angle

An obtuse angle is wide! It is greater than 90° but less than 180°. (Think of a door opened really wide).

4. Straight and Reflex Angles

A Straight Angle measures exactly 180° and forms a perfectly straight line. A Reflex Angle is bent completely backwards! It is greater than 180° but less than 360°.
2D Shapes and Their Properties:
🔶 2D Shapes 🔶

Exploring the flat world of polygons!

1. What is a 2D shape?

A two-dimensional (2D) shape is a flat shape that has length and width, but no thickness! To describe a shape, we look at its sides (straight boundaries) and its vertices (corners where sides meet).

2. What is a Polygon?

A polygon is a closed 2D shape made entirely of straight lines! Triangles, squares, and hexagons are all polygons. A circle is NOT a polygon because it has a curved boundary.

3. The Shape Family

  • Triangle: 3 sides, 3 vertices.
  • Quadrilateral: 4 sides, 4 vertices (Includes Squares and Rectangles!).
  • Pentagon: 5 sides, 5 vertices.
  • Hexagon: 6 sides, 6 vertices (Like a honeycomb!).
  • Octagon: 8 sides, 8 vertices (Like a stop sign!).
Triangles and Their Types:
🔺 Triangles 🔺

The three-sided wonders of geometry!

1. Classifying by Sides

  • Equilateral: All 3 sides are exactly the same length!
  • Isosceles: Exactly 2 sides are the same length.
  • Scalene: Every side is a completely different length!

2. Classifying by Angles

Triangles can also be named by their inside corners!

  • Right-angled: Has one perfect 90° square corner. The longest side is called the hypotenuse!
  • Acute-angled: All three angles are tiny and sharp (less than 90°).
  • Obtuse-angled: Has one very wide angle (greater than 90°).

3. The Magic 180 Rule

No matter what a triangle looks like, if you add up all three of its inside angles, they will ALWAYS equal exactly 180°!
Faces, Edges and Vertices:
🧊 3D Shapes: Faces, Edges, Vertices 🧊

Moving from flat drawings to solid objects you can hold!

1. The 3D Building Blocks

  • Face: A flat surface of a solid shape.
  • Edge: A straight line segment where two faces meet!
  • Vertex: A pointy corner where the edges crash into each other!

2. Let's count them!

  • Cube & Cuboid: 6 Faces, 12 Edges, 8 Vertices!
  • Square-Based Pyramid: 5 Faces, 8 Edges, 5 Vertices (including the pointy top called the Apex).
  • Triangular Prism: 5 Faces (2 triangles, 3 rectangles), 9 Edges, 6 Vertices.

Shapes like spheres and cylinders are special because they have curved surfaces instead of flat polygon faces!
Symmetry and Lines of Symmetry:
🦋 Symmetry 🦋

The beauty of perfect mirror images!

1. What is line symmetry?

A shape has symmetry when a line divides it into two halves that match exactly when you fold one over the other! The halves are perfect mirror images.

2. Lines of Symmetry

A Line of Symmetry is the invisible fold line!

  • A Square has 4 lines of symmetry (Vertical, horizontal, and two diagonals).
  • A Rectangle has 2 (Vertical and horizontal).
  • A Circle has infinite lines! Any line drawn straight through the center works!
  • A shape with NO lines of symmetry is called asymmetrical (like a scalene triangle).
Tessellations and Shape Patterns:
🧩 Tessellations 🧩

Building the perfect puzzle with no empty space!

1. What is a tessellation?

A tessellation is a pattern of shapes that covers a flat surface completely, with NO gaps and NO overlaps! It is like a perfect jigsaw puzzle. You can see them in bathroom tiles, brick walls, and honeycombs!

2. Which shapes work?

Many regular shapes tessellate perfectly by themselves:

  • Squares: They fit in rows and columns perfectly (4 corners of 90° = 360°).
  • Equilateral Triangles: They fit point-to-point!
  • Regular Hexagons: They lock together just like a beehive!

Circles do NOT tessellate by themselves! If you put a bunch of circles together, there will always be empty gaps between them.
